As the first Account Executive, you’ll engage early adopters, work cross-functionally, and contribute to building a repeatable sales motion alongside emerging sales leadership.What you’ll be doingExecute the end-to-end sales lifecycle, from strategic prospecting and initial engagement to complex negotiations and closing.Architect the company’s inaugural sales methodology and playbook, refining the value proposition based on sophisticated market intelligence.Lead comprehensive technical demonstrations and discovery sessions, managing the full technical sales cycle independently.Collaborate with the product and engineering teams to provide critical market feedback, ensuring the product roadmap addresses high-priority customer pain points.Cultivate long-term, trust-based partnerships with CISOs and senior security executives at enterprise-scale organizations.Establish a robust and scalable sales pipeline by leveraging a deep professional network and implementing innovative lead-generation strategies.

jobs.title: Senior AI Systems Engineer, Agents
jobs.location: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, IL
jobs.description: What you'll own﻿Fig's product is built around an AI agent that security analysts and detection engineers work with directly. It investigates coverage questions against live enterprise security data, authors and tests detection logic, and tunes noisy alerting.That agent is already in production with enterprise design partners. Now we need to make it dependable and scalable enough for GA.You will own that evolution: the agent architecture, its evaluation and quality system, and the production engineering around it. This is a hands-on senior IC role with real architectural authority - you set the technical direction and you write the code.The agent operates inside customer security environments, where a wrong action can become a customer incident. Correctness, isolation, observability, and evaluation are not polish. They are the product.What you'll be doing﻿Agent architecture: Design the evolution from today's production single-agent system to a multi-agent one: orchestration, task decomposition, runtime and framework choices, and a migration path that does not break what design partners already rely on.Agent capability: Own the prompts, context, skills, and tool design that make the agent genuinely good at detection engineering across multiple security platforms, not just plausible-sounding.Evaluation platform: Build the harnesses, judges, and golden datasets that turn "the agent feels better" into a number, plus the CI gates that keep regressions from shipping.Reliability and safety: Keep long-running agentic sessions healthy in production, and build the isolation and guardrails required of an agent working inside enterprise security environments.Production debugging: Work real failures from production traces, and turn each one into an eval case that can never regress silently.Technical direction: Make the calls on architecture, sequencing, and quality bar and be accountable for the outcome, including raising how AI-natively the whole team builds.Cross-team partnership: Partner with product and customer-facing teams on what the agent should do, and with platform teams on the data and integrations it depends on.

jobs.title: Senior DevOps Engineer
jobs.location: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, IL
jobs.description: What you'll ownFig's platform runs inside the security stacks of enterprise customers, processing live detection and telemetry data from SIEM, EDR, and SOAR systems at real scale. Until now, infrastructure has been built and carried by the founding engineering team alongside everything else. You will be the first dedicated owner of it. That means designing Fig's cloud foundation across GCP and AWS, building the deployment, scaling, and observability layers from the ground up, and setting the standards the rest of engineering builds on. It also means holding a bar that most startups can defer and Fig cannot: we sell to security teams who audit their vendors seriously, so how we run our own infrastructure is part of how we win. This is a hands-on senior role with real architectural authority, and as engineering grows you become the person others learn cloud and infrastructure from.What you'll be doingMulti-cloud architecture: Own the design and implementation of Fig's multi-cloud architecture across GCP and AWS, including the cross-cloud standards, boundaries, and tradeoffs that keep two providers from becoming twice the complexity.Infrastructure as code: Build and maintain the entire environment in Terraform, so infrastructure is reviewable, reproducible, and scales without a person in the loop.Deployment pipelines from scratch: Create the CI/CD foundation that lets a small team ship quickly and safely, with the testing, gating, and rollback paths that make fast releases boring rather than risky.Kubernetes at data scale: Run and scale the Kubernetes and containerized workloads behind Fig's security data processing, where volume, latency, and cost pressure all show up at once.Security of our own stack: Own identity, access, secrets, network boundaries, and infrastructure hardening to a standard that holds up under customer security review.Reliability and visibility: Build the logging, monitoring, and alerting layer that tells us something is wrong before a customer does, and make on-call sustainable as the system grows.Technical direction: Partner directly with the founding engineering team on architectural decisions, and raise the infrastructure and cloud fluency of every engineer who joins after you.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.location: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, IL
jobs.description: What you'll ownFig's product does the work a SecOps engineer does: it investigates coverage gaps against live enterprise security data, authors and tests detection logic, and tunes noisy alerting. That means product decisions here are SecOps engineering decisions, and they need someone who has actually done the job. You'll join Fig's product team and own the detection engineering surface of the product - what good coverage analysis looks like, what correct detection content looks like, what a security team should be able to trust the product to do on its own. Fig is defining a category around Security Operations Resilience, and the fastest way to get that right is to be genuinely credible with the SecOps engineers we're building for.What you'll be doingDrive the detection product domain: Bring deep expertise in SecOps engineering across SIEM, data pipelines, and SOAR, and help the product team define where the product should excel. Develop a strong understanding of the day-to-day work of SecOps engineers and the challenges they face.Turn expertise into product insight: Conduct deep, hands-on research across real security environments, SecOps engineering practices, data, and tooling. Combine customer feedback with your own experience and the knowledge of the broader team to identify meaningful problems, opportunities, and product directions.Shape and execute the roadmap: Translate product insights into a focused roadmap aligned with company strategy and customer needs. Partner with the product and engineering teams to prioritize initiatives, make tradeoffs, define outcomes, and drive execution from discovery through delivery.Turn problems into product direction: Translate ambiguous problems into clear product requirements and actionable plans. Work closely with engineering, design, and security experts to ensure complex technical problems are translated into products that are useful, intuitive, and technically sound.Shape and evaluate AI agent capabilities: Define what Fig’s AI agent should be capable of doing as a SecOps engineer, what good looks like, and where it must be trusted or constrained. Develop evaluation frameworks, scenarios, and ground truth to measure and continuously improve agent performance.Own product quality and outcomes: Maintain a deep understanding of how the product is used in real-world security operations. Validate assumptions, identify gaps, and use customer feedback, product data, and operational experience to continuously improve the product and its direction.
